title: Guardrails and safety controls
task_statement: Enforce guardrails in code with input checks, tool gates, and a sandbox boundary. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Input validation and untrusted-content handling
components.first_principle: A prompt is guidance. Code checks user input and labels third-party content before the model acts on it.

nodes.label: Harmlessness screen on a lightweight model
Email, web page, or file content

steps: Screen each user message with a lightweight model before the main call.
Use structured outputs so the screen returns a parseable boolean.
Treat a refusal stop reason on the screen as a harmful verdict.
Place third-party content only in tool_result blocks, never in system prompts.
Label the source of that content so the model can judge how far to trust it.
State in the system prompt that tool content is untrusted data and must not override instructions.
Test the workflow with documents that carry injected instructions.
pros: Blocks many direct injection attempts before the main model call.
Keeps untrusted content in tool results, where Claude treats embedded instructions with skepticism.
Produces a verdict that the application can log and count.
cons: A screen adds a model call and latency to each screened request.
A screen can miss new attack wording, so it is not a complete control.
A screen can block a legitimate request.
use_when: Users type free text that reaches the model.
The model reads email, web pages, or files from third parties.
Tool results contain text that other people wrote.
do_not_use_when: The input is fixed text that your own team wrote.
The goal is to stop a tool call. Use a deterministic gate instead.

constraints.choice: Use a small model for the screen, not the main model.
constraints.combination: Add the screen only to routes that accept untrusted text. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Log each screen verdict with its request ID.
constraints.combination: Throttle or ban users who repeat the same refusal, after review.

constraints.choice: Monitor screen verdicts and tool-result flags over time.
constraints.combination: Refine the screen prompt when misses or false positives appear.

constraints.choice: Write the screen prompt with examples of known injection language.

native_services.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails filter content for Claude Code. The guardrail headers go in the settings file.

components.exam_tie: D5.1. Expect a scenario where untrusted text reaches the model. The credited answer screens and labels the input. Prompt wording alone does not count. (Inference)
components.trap: A stricter system prompt as the only control. The model can still follow an injected instruction, and no code stops the action.
components.decision_rule: Screen untrusted text before the main call, and keep third-party content in tool_result blocks.
components.exam_tip: If the only defense is prompt wording, add an input screen or a code check.

components.name: Deterministic tool authorization gate
components.first_principle: Code that runs the tool decides whether the call proceeds, so the model cannot override the decision.
steps: The model proposes a tool call with arguments.
The gate checks the call against rules that live in code or settings.
Claude Code evaluates deny rules first, then ask rules, then allow rules.
A PreToolUse hook can block the call before the tool runs.
A hook that exits with code 2 blocks the call, even when its JSON output allows it.
The tool runs only when every check allows the call.
pros: Enforces the rule outside the model, so a prompt cannot override it.
Puts deny rules before allow rules, so a broad deny wins.
Runs a custom hook on each tool call that a matcher selects.
cons: Each rule needs upkeep when tools or limits change.
A broad deny rule can block legitimate work.
Hook scripts run outside the sandbox and need their own review.
use_when: A tool moves money, changes data, or sends messages.
The limit is a value or a list that code can check.
The control must hold when the prompt is attacked.
do_not_use_when: The tool is read-only and public, so no side effect needs a gate.
The check needs a person to decide each case. Use a review step instead.

constraints.choice: Set a bare deny rule for a tool that the workflow never needs.
constraints.combination: Use a pattern deny rule when only some arguments are unsafe.

constraints.choice: Set disableBypassPermissionsMode to disable in managed settings.
constraints.combination: Set disableAutoMode the same way when auto mode must stay off.

constraints.choice: Give each agent only the tool scopes that its task needs.
constraints.combination: Limit a key's permissions at the service that issued it. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Set a permission policy for each toolset in the agent configuration.
constraints.combination: Use a custom tool when your own code must own the check.

native_services.text: Not in source. The permission and hook pages name no cloud platform for this control.

components.exam_tie: D5.1. Expect a scenario where a tool moves money or data and a prompt is the only control. The credited answer adds a code gate that fails closed. (Inference)
components.trap: A longer prompt that says the model must not call the tool. The model can still propose the call, and only code blocks it.
components.decision_rule: Enforce each limit for a tool with side effects in code, before the call runs.
components.exam_tip: If a system prompt sentence is the only check on a limit, the design needs a code gate.

components.name: Sandbox boundary for shell commands
components.first_principle: A boundary enforced by the host limits what a shell command can reach, even when injected content steers the command.
steps: Run /sandbox in a Claude Code session to turn on the sandbox.
The sandbox limits writes to the current directory, a per-user temp directory, and added directories.
The sandbox sends outbound requests through a proxy that checks each host.
The proxy allows only the hosts on the allowed domain list.
Read access covers most of the machine by default, so add deny read rules for credential files.
File tools, MCP servers, and hooks run outside the sandbox, so they need their own rules.
pros: Limits what a shell command can reach, even after an injection.
Blocks direct network routes by default.
Needs no change to the model prompt.
cons: Covers shell commands only, so file and web tools need permission rules.
Read access covers most of the machine by default.
Native Windows runs commands without the sandbox. Use WSL2 instead.
use_when: The agent runs shell commands on a developer machine or in a container.
Untrusted input can lead to a shell command.
The task needs only a few known hosts.
do_not_use_when: The agent never runs shell commands.
The host is native Windows without WSL2. Run the agent in a container or VM instead.

constraints.choice: Limit writes to the current directory and the directories you add.
constraints.combination: Add deny write rules for shared configuration files.

constraints.choice: Keep the allowed domain list empty until a task needs a host.
constraints.combination: Add a host only after a review of its data handling. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use strict sandbox mode for tasks that touch untrusted input.
constraints.combination: Set failIfUnavailable so that commands do not run unsandboxed when the sandbox cannot start.

constraints.choice: Review each request to retry a command outside the sandbox.

native_services.text: Not in source. The sandbox pages name no cloud platform setting for this boundary.

components.exam_tie: D5.1. Expect a scenario where a shell command could reach credentials or an unknown host. The credited answer names a sandbox with an allowed domain list. (Inference)
components.trap: A team turns the sandbox on and believes it covers file tools or hooks. The sandbox wraps shell commands only.
components.decision_rule: Use the sandbox for shell commands, and use permission rules for file and web tools.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario asks about the Read tool, the sandbox does not apply to that tool.

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Untrusted text reaches the model?} -->|Yes| B[Screen input and label tool results]
  A -->|No| C{Action has side effects?}
  B --> C
  C -->|Yes| D[Code gate on the tool call]
  C -->|No| E[Read-only tool with permission rule]
  D --> F{Shell command involved?}
  E --> F
  F -->|Yes| G[Sandbox with empty allowed domain list]
  F -->|No| H[Deny by default for other tools]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  P[Prompt is guidance] --> G[Code gate]
  G --> R[Deny rule first]
  R --> K[Hook exit 2 blocks]
  U[Untrusted content] --> S[Input screen]
  U --> T[tool_result block]
  B[Shell command] --> X[Sandbox]
  X --> D[Empty domain list]

patterns.wording: a model follows a prompt sentence that forbids a limited action
patterns.answer_type: code gate on the tool call
patterns.rule: Enforce the limit in code. Keep the prompt sentence as guidance only.
traps: Longer system prompt with more warnings
Remove the tool and lose the function

patterns.wording: instructions appear inside a document that the agent reads
patterns.answer_type: untrusted-content handling plus a tool gate
patterns.rule: Label and screen the content. Keep the gate on every tool the content could steer.
traps: Trust a document because the company stored it

patterns.wording: a shell command could read credentials or reach an unknown host
patterns.answer_type: sandbox boundary with an empty allowed domain list
patterns.rule: Limit shell reach by default. Add hosts and paths only when a task needs them.
traps: Add every host to avoid prompts
Assume the sandbox covers file tools
